user.title: iPhone Alarms Sync
user.description:
Choose how to add your iPhone/iPad:

- **Mobile App device** - links it to your Home Assistant app device
- **Custom name** - standalone device

select_mobile_app.title: Select Mobile App Device
select_mobile_app.description: Select your device from Mobile App integration.

custom_name.title: Enter Device Name
custom_name.description:
Enter a name for your iPhone/iPad (e.g., "John's iPhone").

This generates a **Phone ID** needed for the shortcut setup.

confirm.title: Set up the Sync shortcut
confirm.description:
**Phone ID:** `{phone_id}`

## 1. Import the Sync shortcut

Scan the QR code or open the link **on the iPhone/iPad you are adding**:

![QR Code]({sync_qr_code})

[Open Shortcut]({sync_shortcut_url})

Import questions:
- **Phone ID**: `{phone_id}`
- **Home Wi-Fi** (optional): fill in only if Home Assistant works just at home
- **Server** and **Action**: your Home Assistant server, then `iphone_alarms_sync.sync_alarms`

If the **Perform action** step shows **Choose** or the shortcut says *No server provided*, pick the **Server** and then the **Action** again (needs the Home Assistant app 2026.9.3+, [troubleshooting]({troubleshooting_url})).

## 2. Create the automation

1. Shortcuts app → Automation → +
2. App → Clock → Is Closed
3. Run Shortcut → "iPhone Alarms Sync: Sync"
4. Enable "Run Immediately" → Done

Alarms then sync every time you close the Clock app.

## 3. Event shortcuts (optional)

To react when an alarm goes off, is snoozed or stopped, set up the event shortcuts afterwards in **Configure → Event Shortcuts Setup**.

event_shortcuts.title: Event Shortcuts Setup
event_shortcuts.description:
**Phone ID:** `{phone_id}`

## Alarm IDs

{alarms_list}

The Alarm Event shortcut asks for one of these IDs.

## Device Event shortcut

Reports events of **any alarm**, the **Wake-Up alarm** and **sleep** (bedtime, wind down, waking up).

![QR Code]({device_event_qr_code})

[Open Shortcut]({device_event_shortcut_url})

Import questions:
- **Phone ID**: `{phone_id}`
- **Home Wi-Fi** (optional): fill in only if Home Assistant works just at home
- **Event Type Number**:
  - 1-3: any alarm (goes off, snoozed, stopped)
  - 4-6: Wake-Up alarm (goes off, snoozed, stopped)
  - 7: waking up
  - 8: wind down starts
  - 9: bedtime starts
- **Server** and **Action**: your Home Assistant server, then `iphone_alarms_sync.report_device_event`

## Alarm Event shortcut

Reports events of **one alarm**.

![QR Code]({alarm_event_qr_code})

[Open Shortcut]({alarm_event_shortcut_url})

Import questions:
- **Phone ID**: `{phone_id}`
- **Home Wi-Fi** (optional): fill in only if Home Assistant works just at home
- **Alarm ID**: from the list above
- **Event Type Number**: 1 (goes off), 2 (snoozed) or 3 (stopped)
- **Server** and **Action**: your Home Assistant server, then `iphone_alarms_sync.report_alarm_event`

## Automation

One copy of a shortcut sends one event, so import it once per event. For each copy:

1. Shortcuts app → Automation → +
2. Choose the trigger, for example "When Alarm Goes Off"
3. Run Shortcut → the copy you imported
4. Enable "Run Immediately" → Done

If the **Perform action** step shows **Choose** or the shortcut says *No server provided*, pick the **Server** and then the **Action** again (needs the Home Assistant app 2026.9.3+, [troubleshooting]({troubleshooting_url})).

no_data.title: {phone_name} stopped sending alarm data
no_data.description:
{phone_name} hasn't sent anything to iPhone Alarms Sync for {days} days.

This usually means the iOS shortcuts stopped working, for example after a Home Assistant app update reset the **Action** field of the **Perform action** step.

1. Open the Shortcuts app and run the Sync shortcut manually.
2. If it shows an error, *No server provided* or **Choose** in the Perform action step, pick the **Server** and then `iphone_alarms_sync.sync_alarms` as the **Action** (or re-import the shortcuts from the integration options).
3. Check the same in the event shortcuts.

This issue disappears automatically when the phone sends data again. If you rarely open the Clock app, you can ignore it.
